newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sellers slash Australian stocks by close.
newsitem.headline: Sellers slash Australian stocks by close.

text.p: The Australian share market closed lower on Friday as traders succumbed to the temptation to take profits after the run to record highs.
The All Ordinaries index lost 13.8 points to 2,482.6.

The day started out on a much more bullish note, however, with the benchmark All Ordinaries index hitting a record and intraday high of 2,506.5 in early trade before profit-takers pushed it down to its closing level.

"It got hit pretty hard, the SPI (Share Price Index futures) especially, but there was nothing in particular triggering it," said dealer Phillip Toop of Brisbane-based brokerage, Lance Jones, adding that the losses were widespread after the recent foray above the 2,500 level.
"The selling has come through across the board. CRA got hit and the banks were generally a touch softer."

The results season continued apace with Perth casino owner and operator Burswood Property Trust the first cab off the rank, reporting an 84 percent higher first half net profit of A$25.2 million (US$19.2 million). It was not enough, however, to stop its units closing four cents lower at A$1.61.

Industrial conglomerate Pacific Dunlop edged higher to A$3.16 despite a 27.6 percent lower first half net profit of A$84.46 million. Soft drink maker C-C Amatil reported a slightly higher full year net profit of A$142.1 million after trading closed. Its shares added 20.2 cents to A$13.657.

Biscuit maker Arnotts Ltd reported a 14.2 percent lower net profit before abnormals of A$33.2 million and its shares closed 25 cents weaker at A$8.50. However, an extortion threat that saw supermarkets remove Arnotts products from their shelves was the main news influencing the stock today, rather than the profit figure, brokers said.
Newspaper group John Fairfax Holdings reported a 24.7 percent lower first half net profit of A$46.95 million after the close. Its shares lost seven cents to A$3.03.

Mt Leyshon Gold Mines, part of the Normandy Mining group, ended unchanged at A$2.29 in thin trade after its 13.8 percent lower first half net profit of A$9.36 million. Fellow group member North Flinders Mines reported a 16.8 percent lower first half net profit of A$14.48 million, its shares ending 85 cents higher at A$7.85 after only three trades.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about nine to eight, while about 28 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
